vol_label_shape_stats — VOLCOLOR measure op

• Data kinds: labels → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.vol_label_shape_stats(labels, spacing=None, shape: 'bool' = True) (to call the implementation directly, import volcolor; volcolor.vol_label_shape_stats(labels, spacing=None, shape: 'bool' = True); from the registry, opsvolcolor.get("vol_label_shape_stats"))

Usage

Per-component quantities that can be had in linear time (volume, centroid, box, PCA shape indices).

Sister of volops.vol_region_props, but with a different purpose:

• It gives out surface_area and Wadell sphericity. For that purpose Since the marching cubes are run for each component, the Python loop is proportional to the number of components. Turn** (quickly becomes heavy with pathological input of 1 voxel 1 label). * This is limited to the amount that requires only the weighted sum of np.bincount. 1 label array 10 bincount(number of pieces 1, coordinate sum 3, covariance 6) = O(N + n). Actual measurement (connectivity=26, Checkerboard pattern of 1 voxel 1 label = pathological input): 16**3 = 4096 voxels / 512 components = 0.0037 s, 32**3 = 32768 / 4096 = 0.0350 s, 64**3 = 262144 / 32768 = 0.2556 s, 128**3 = 2097152 / 262144 = 2.3122 s. 9.5 / 7.3 / 9.0 times for every 8 voxels (64 times for quadratic), Approximately 1.1 microseconds/voxel over the entire area. The same 128**3 coloring is 0.0357 s. (For reference: volops.vol_region_props(surface="faces") is the same 16**3 0.0121 s -- 3.5 times longer due to the Python loop for each component. marching cubes The default to use surface="auto" is even heavier. )

label voxel_count volume centroid bbox volops.vol_region_props same definition and same value (tests/test_volcolor.py::test_stats_agree_with_vol_region_props_exactly is (fixed with exact match). bbox is (z0, z1, y0, y1, x0, x1) and the upper limit is exclusive.

What we also return:

centroid_mm (z, y, x) Physical coordinates (same as voxel without spacing)

extent Physical dimensions of bbox (dz, dy, dx) · equivalent_diameter

(6V/pi)**(1/3) · touches_border Does bbox touch the volume edge? ·

principal_extent Square root of covariance eigenvalue (s1 >= s2 >= s3)(physical unit) ·

linearity (l1-l2)/l1 · planarity (l2-l3)/l1 · isotropy

l3/l1 · elongation sqrt(l1/l2).

elongation can be infinite (contract): l1 > 0 and l2 == 0, In other words, a perfectly straight line component with a thickness of 1 voxel returns inf. Accident divided by 0 Rather, it is the fact that there is no spread in the second axis direction, and when rounded, the order of slenderness changes. They switch places silently. A single voxel (l1 == 0) is an isotropic point, so it is 1.0.

If you forget to pass spacing, the numbers and conclusions will change. Actual measurement - A sphere with a radius of 6 mm spacing = (3.0, 1.0, 1.0) When sampled with an anisotropic grid of mm (3 times coarser in z), It becomes 293 voxels. The closed-form true value is 4/3 pi 6**3 = 904.78 mm**3:

• With spacing = 879.0 mm**3 (error -2.85 %), isotropy = 0.7349 (approximately isotropic = correct).

• No spacing = 293.0 (in voxel units. Error -67.62% when read as mm**3), isotropy = 0.0817 -- The sphere looks like a "board". Ignoring anisotropy The shape index is broken, yet returns a finite and reasonable value.

*Equivalent diameter also differs by a factor of 1.44, 11.8849 mm vs. 8.2406.

Numerical note: The second moment is calculated as E[x**2] - E[x]**2, so the coordinates For components with large and small spreads, loss of precision may occur. Upper limit MAX_COLOR_VOXELS (up to ~2000 on one side), the relative precision of float64 for E[x**2] ~ 4e6 is 1e-16 = Absolute 1e-10, with 10 orders of magnitude margin for voxel-wise variance. bigger than that The volume should be passed after cutting the ROI (this is also the reason for the upper limit).

Setting *shape* to False will omit the covariance (bincount of 6 out of 10), principal_extent Do not return the following 5 items -- only volumetric filters are required Sometimes an O(N) temporary array can be reduced to one.

Returns list[dict] in ascending label order (actual labels only) --- labels.max() does not return an empty dict even if there are gaps in the number).
